name: codebase_search
description: Search literal text, case-insensitively, in repository file contents (not filenames). Excludes config, node_modules and .git. Returns query, query_valid, count (all matching lines), shown, results (path, line, excerpt), truncated, and index_age. Zero matches is success with count=0 and query_valid=true; an empty/whitespace query, query over 200 characters, or malformed path glob is an error. Defaults to concise: at most 10 hits with 160-character excerpts; detailed allows 20 hits with 500-character excerpts. truncated indicates omitted matches or shortened excerpts. index_age reports how old the index is, or live disk for deep search.

query.description: Literal text to find, 1–200 characters and not whitespace-only. Use a distinctive code term or error string; broad terms consume more result space.

max_results.description: Maximum matching lines, 1–20; null uses 10. Smaller limits save context; concise additionally caps results at 10.

path_glob.description: Restrict matching repository-relative paths using a glob such as src/*.ts; null searches all indexed paths. Supports *, ?, brackets and {a,b}; no SQL, free-text filter syntax, absolute paths or .. segments. Restriction reduces results.

deep.description: False uses the cheaper prebuilt index; true scans current files from disk, costing more local I/O. Choose true when index age makes freshness uncertain.

response_format.description: Choose concise by default to save context; detailed returns more code when the shorter result is insufficient.

examples.note: Typical: begin with a cheap indexed literal-text search, the default ten-result limit, and no path restriction.

Hard case: if earlier results were truncated and the index may be stale, search current TypeScript files with a larger result budget. The glob filters paths; query still searches file contents. This costs more disk I/O and context; zero matches remains a valid result.
